title: Cohort-driven perturbation eval & auto-threshold synthesis for quant profiles
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: build an automated evaluation flow that measures quality regressions introduced by quantization profiles (int8/int4, AWQ/GPTQ) along cohort-specific failure modes and synthesizes per-profile thresholds that can be used as rollout gates.

Motivation: existing delta-based checks flag overall metric drops but miss cohort-sensitive regressions (e.g., long-form summarization, instruction-following, numeric reasoning). We need a finer-grained, perturbation-driven test harness that: 1) enumerates targeted perturbations (per-layer noise, weight pruning, KV-cache stress), 2) quantifies sensitivity per cohort and prompt archetype, and 3) automatically proposes thresholds balancing quality risk vs unit-cost gains. The output must integrate with the pipeline that blocks or allows model/config rollouts (canary, A/B).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Perturbation harness implemented in eval pipeline that can inject per-layer, per-block, and global weight perturbations for AWQ/GPTQ profiles
A2: Cohort definitions stored and versioned; at minimum cohorts for: short completion, long completion, multi-turn chat, few-shot code, numeric reasoning
A3: Auto-threshold synthesizer produces a recommended threshold for a model+profile+cohort tuple and outputs expected quality delta and cost savings
A4: Dashboard visualizing sensitivity heatmaps (layers x cohorts) and ROC-like tradeoff curves for threshold selection
A5: Integration with rollout gate: when synthesized threshold is exceeded for any high-risk cohort, the rollout is blocked and detailed findings are posted to the release ticket
A6: End-to-end tests and a smoke job run on every release pipeline with synthetic perturbations to detect regressions in the harness itself
tasks: T1: Design perturbation taxonomy and CLI for selecting perturbation types (per-layer gaussian noise, block zeroing, weight quant noise)
T2: Implement driver that applies AWQ/GPTQ profile variations and runs evals across cohorts (extend existing eval-harness)
T3: Build threshold synthesizer: collect metrics, compute pareto frontier of cost vs quality, propose threshold and confidence band
T4: Export sensitivity heatmaps and threshold artifacts to console/CDP for human review
T5: Create rollout-gate backend hook that accepts the synthesizer verdict and prevents canary promotion if gating conditions met
T6: Add unit/integration tests and schedule nightly calibration runs on representative workloads
T7: Write runbook and onboarding doc for PM/SEs describing how to interpret threshold recommendations
notes: Implementation approach: start with a lightweight perturbation runner that reuses tokenization and scoring from the existing eval-harness. We prioritize per-cohort aggregated deltas (BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore where applicable and instruction-success for chat) and then fit a simple cost-quality model (linear-interpolation then convex hull) to propose thresholds. If curves are noisy, apply bootstrapped confidence intervals. Thresholds are accompanied by an "explain" artifact listing top failing prompts and per-layer contributors.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12 Maya Chen: Initial spec complete; confirmed core cohorts with PM (short/long/multi-turn/code/numeric).
2026-02-18 Luca Moretti: Perturbation runner prototype added to feature/perturbation-harness branch. Local smoke tests for AWQ int8 profiles passed on small LLaMA-2 curve dataset.
2026-02-24 Maya Chen: Ran cohort sweep on gpt-7b-open weights; observed layer 10-14 high sensitivity for long-form summarization. Drafted heatmap prototype exported to console.

2026-03-02 Omar Rodriguez (review): Suggested adding a noise-floor calibration step and to prefer relative delta metrics for high-variance cohorts. Also recommended storing raw per-prompt scores for auditability.
2026-03-07 Luca Moretti: Implemented basic threshold synthesizer; chooses knee-point on cost-quality curve and emits confidence band via bootstrap (100 resamples).
2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Hooked synthesizer output into rollout-gate prototype; can now block promotion in CI. Next: finalize dashboards and run overnight calibration on representative fleet.
review_feedback: Omar Rodriguez: Important to include example-based explanations for any blocked rollout. Engineers need the minimal failing prompt set to reproduce locally.
Aisha Patel (PM): Make sure thresholds are surfaced as recommendations with manual override and an audit trail for compliance.
R&D (K. Singh): For AWQ profiles, consider quantization-aware perturbations (simulate group-wise scaling) rather than naive gaussian noise. This improves signal fidelity.
decisions: D1: Use cohort-first evaluations (grouped prompts) rather than global aggregates for gating
D2: Default synthesizer algorithm: find Pareto frontier then select knee-point by maximizing curvature; fallback to fixed delta threshold when data noisy
D3: All synthesized thresholds will be emitted with a 95% bootstrap confidence interval and top-10 failing prompts artifact
D4: Gate will be advisory for P2/P3 releases and blocking for P0/P1 releases by default
risks: R1: False positives blocking rollouts due to noisy cohorts — mitigated by bootstrap CIs and manual override
R2: Compute cost of running full perturbation sweeps across many profiles may be high — mitigate with sampled cohorts and nightly calibration rather than per-PR full runs
R3: AWQ/GPTQ simulation mismatch — need to validate that the perturbation modes faithfully reflect quant behavior on target hardware
